question_36499753002: At Arborphy AI I do model-level work on transformer-based vision models for plant species identification. I built a plant species classifier on about 9,000 images spanning 200+ species, designing an EfficientNet–BioCLIP dual-encoder with bidirectional spatial cross-attention and BioCLIP-anchored gated residuals, and improved fusion macro-F1 from 0.808 to 0.832 across architecture iterations. I designed a leakage-aware evaluation protocol (individual-disjoint splits, multi-seed runs, grouped held-out sets) and benchmarked frozen BioCLIP, DINOv3 and EfficientNet embeddings with linear probes and cross-species retrieval; DINOv3 reached 87.3% organ-classification accuracy. This is applied work in an early-stage product rather than a large-scale production deployment.
question_37586354002: I have not yet owned a direct external enterprise-customer engagement on an ML/AI problem, so I would not want to overstate that. The closest analogue is stakeholder-facing ML work where the users were domain experts rather than ML engineers. At Columbia Zuckerman, after building self-supervised denoising workflows for two-photon calcium-imaging data, I organized the research code into a downloadable package and wrote step-by-step documentation for wet-lab researchers. I also presented survey-analysis findings to board members at the Columbia Asian Faculty Association. For Databricks AI FDE, I would bring that same habit of translating model behavior, evaluation tradeoffs, and implementation details into decisions a customer can act on, while continuing to build direct enterprise-facing experience.
